To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk of long lasting ventriculomegelia is increased in newborns with moderate hypoxic brain damage, if they have the following factors: morphofunctional brain immaturity, absence of compensatory reduced resistance index in anterior brain arteries, metabolic acidosis and activation of carbonhydrase in urine.

the presence of the risk factors of the development of long remaining ventricolomegalia in newborns with moderate perinatal brain injury is: the morphological immaturity of the central nervous sytem (CNS), absence of compensative reduced resistance index (RI), metabolic acidosis and carbanhydrase activiation.

ventriculomegelia is a common complication of moderate perinatal hypoxic damage of newborns, and the markers of its development are the morphofunctionally immaturity of brain, the absence of compensatory reaction of the brain arteries, metabolic acidosis and carbanhydrase activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a prospective examination of 123 children with hypoxic brain damage of moderate degree of severity.

the necessity to perform neurosonographic examination of all newborns with hypoxia of the central nervous systems and to use the dopplerography of anterior brain arteries in children with ventriculomagaly for early detection of the compensatory reduction of RI.
the development of the algorithm of the early diagnostics and treatment of newborns with periventricular damage of moderate severity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of diacarb in the treatment of newborns with ventriculomelia should be limited.
ventriculomegaly is a marker of the severity of brain damage, which is associated with metabolic acidosis and the immaturity of the central nervous and renal systems.
diacarb is not indicated in newborns with moderate brain damage and ventriculomegaly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the newborns with periventricular damage of moderate severity, ventriculomegaly is a frequent finding, which is associated with metabolic and functional disorders of the central nervous and renal systems.

the newborns with hypoxia of moderate severity and with the risk factors for the development of the hydrocephaly should be examined by neurosonography and dopplerography on 4-5 days after birth and in the case of the detected ventriculomegaly - the treatment with diacarb should be prescribed.

the newborns with periventricular hypoxic damage of moderate severity have a higher risk of ventriculomegaly and the markers of its development are the morphofunctionally immature brain, absence of compensatory reduced resistance index in the anterior brain arteries on the 4th-7th day of life, metabolic acidosis, carbanhydrase activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is necessary to conduct the early neurosonographic examination in newborns with survived perinatal hypoxia and the presence of the risk factors for hydrocephaly in order to determine the necessity of diacarb administration.
the use of diacarb for newborns with ventriculomelia is not justified.
the risk of ventriculomegaly is increased in newborns with hypoxia of moderate severity.
